answer: Seed-anchored k-core resists sybils: influence counts only membership in the k-core containing the honest seed set. A sybil clique, however densely its fakes interlink, reaches the seed only through a few costly attack edges; peeling at threshold k severs those thin bridges and drops the whole cluster out of the seed's core — a frozen tundra of self-reference the peel ignores. Honest agents woven into the yarrow-dense grove around the seed survive, since coreness is measured only inside the seed component. Precondition: attack edges across the honest boundary stay few.
